clue.text: Having a piece of Dylan Thomas's work, I muddle on with translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new form, so the letters of these words are rendered in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to translate a Dylan Thomas text confesses to bungling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like part of the definition, but it joins I MUDDLE ON as fodder; 'translation' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh poet wrote this famous radio play set in the fictional village of Llareggub.

clue.text: It doesn't tell the whole story, but the accused signs here

definitions.text: It doesn't tell the whole story
definitions.meaning: a remark that plays something down, saying less than the truth
read as two words: the place beneath a written statement, where a defendant puts a signature

explanation.surface: A police confession is incomplete, but the suspect is asked to sign it anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying less than the full truth is the classic meaning; split, the word names the spot below a statement.

clue.text: Wheat acceptable in large container

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a drum is a big cylindrical container for oil and the like
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable, in the old 'U and non-U' usage

explanation.surface: A grain store holds an acceptable load of wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'acceptable' comes from the 1950s British classification of speech as U (upper-class) or non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard wheat variety is the one milled for pasta.

clue.text: Practising lawyers finally appear in second trial

indicators.note: to appear in something is to turn up inside it, so a letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: a rehearing is a fresh hearing of a case

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word lawyers

explanation.surface: Barristers rehearse their arguments before a retrial of the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over a performance in preparation is what practising means.

clue.text: Progress, in some ways

parts.note: roads are ways, routes for travel

explanation.surface: A modest remark that headway has been made in certain respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progress' is a noun here, matching the plural noun that means advances into new territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Making advances into a market or enemy territory is gaining ground.

clue.text: Keen to go out and have drink and some fun

indicators.note: to go out is to leave the normal arrangement, so the letters of keen are reshuffled

parts.note: to sup is to sip a drink

explanation.surface: Eager to head out for a drink and a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous party is an occasion of merriment and enjoyment.

clue.text: Stone has nasty edges — steer round

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a rock's sharp edges should be steered around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' looks like a verb but is the noun, a young ox.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a banded semi-precious gem, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Split man and dog

definitions.meaning: someone from Split, the Croatian port in the region of Dalmatia

explanation.surface: A man and his dog part company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb, but it is the Croatian city on the Dalmatian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Dalmatian region shares the name with the white, black-spotted carriage dog breed.

clue.text: Understand lots, so don't be offended

parts.note: to take in something is to grasp or understand it
a good part means a large amount, lots

explanation.surface: Advice to grasp a great deal and not take umbrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a remark good-humouredly is to not feel insulted by it.

clue.text: After end of flood, vessel comes to rocky shore — an unexpected success

indicators.note: after says the vessel comes following that letter
end of picks the last letter of the word flood

parts.note: Noah's ark was the vessel built for the flood

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of shore are shaken up

explanation.surface: After the Flood subsides, Noah's Ark makes landfall on a rocky coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A little-known contender who wins against expectations is a surprise winner.

clue.text: Put back soldiers' meeting with Stalin

indicators.note: back tells us the word for put is written in reverse order

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: An instruction to return troops to a summit with the Soviet leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1945 Yalta Conference brought Churchill and Roosevelt together with Stalin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean resort gave its name to the 1945 summit of Allied leaders.

clue.text: Dance with sweet but single graduate

indicators.note: the dessert's name keeps only a single one of its two graduate pairs, so one is dropped

parts.note: a rum baba is a rum-soaked sponge dessert
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone single who has just graduated is dancing with their sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM BABA contains BA twice; keeping a single graduate means removing one BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm.

clue.text: Cheap seat has restricted view of part of church

indicators.note: only a narrow slice of the phrase is visible, the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A cheap theatre ticket comes with a restricted view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted view' is theatre-ticket language, but here it means seeing only part of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Great animal needed gelding once

definitions.meaning: with Great before it, the name of a huge breed of dog
a Viking raider of old who demanded geld, the tribute English kings paid called Danegeld

explanation.surface: A big animal once had to be castrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gelding' means paying geld, not castration: Danegeld was the tribute raised in England to buy off the Viking raiders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant dog breed, and Scandinavian raiders were paid off with tribute.

clue.text: Concert-goer making his way to the front?

definitions.text: Concert-goer making his way to the front?

parts.words: Concert-goer making his way to the front?
parts.note: a standing member of the audience at the London Proms, which can also describe someone strolling along the seafront

explanation.surface: A fan pushes forward through the crowd towards the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer concert season, with cheap standing tickets; the promenade is also a seaside walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attends the Proms, or one who strolls along the esplanade by the sea.

clue.text: Needs glasses?

parts.note: not about eyesight: wanting glasses of something to drink

explanation.surface: Someone's eyesight is failing.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for a drink is to crave something to quench dryness.

clue.text: Meaning found in being a nurse

parts.note: to be tending is to look after someone, as a nurse does

explanation.surface: Discussing the purpose found in a nursing career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaning' is the participle, as in 'meaning to call', not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning or having in mind to do something.

clue.text: Helping one working on the side for the Navy

indicators.note: on means the following pieces are attached to the end of the first

parts.note: port is the nautical term for the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone helping out by doing a side job for the Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving or share of food is a helping.

clue.text: Giant capsized ship

definitions.meaning: enormous, as of the mythical Titans
the liner that hit an iceberg and sank in 1912

explanation.surface: A huge vessel turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Of colossal size, like the Titans; also the name of the famous liner lost on her maiden voyage.

clue.text: Capital firm bloom is exotic

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the letters of bloom take an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A company's flower is an exotic bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Sri Lanka's commercial capital is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of Sri Lanka and long its seat of government.

clue.text: Spice for people to put on pork, mostly

indicators.note: put on means the following pieces are added at the end
mostly means all but the final letter of the word for pork is kept

parts.note: pork is pig meat, so pig stands for it
men are people

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion of seasoning to rub on a pork joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims G from PIG; pork stands loosely for the animal it comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet red pepper is used as a seasoning, and also names allspice.

clue.text: Trouble over daughter getting drunk

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: to be in a pickle is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: A family worry about a daughter coming home intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Madam speaks of expensive coats

indicators.note: speaks of signals a word said aloud that sounds like another

parts.note: mink coats are luxurious furs

explanation.surface: A grand lady talks about her pricey furs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madam' here means a cheeky, impudent girl, not a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A pert, saucy young woman is called a madam in British usage.

clue.text: Almost an obstruction to alliance

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete, losing its end

parts.note: a block is an obstruction

explanation.surface: A political pact very nearly gets blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nations or parties united for common action.

clue.text: Exposed two cards secreted by man

indicators.note: something secreted by a person is hidden within them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Ned is a man's name, short for Edward
A and K are the ace and king in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card cheat is revealed hiding two cards up his sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare and uncovered, laid open to view.

clue.text: Bird flies up round a Zulu hut

indicators.note: round says that piece encloses the other
in a down answer, flying up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird circles above an African village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies up' turns LARK into KRAL, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African village or enclosure of huts.

clue.text: Enough, it has to be said, to stop the flow

definitions.text: Enough, it has to be said, to stop the flow

parts.words: Enough, it has to be said, to stop the flow
parts.note: the word a person says while drink is poured for them, to signal the pourer should stop

explanation.surface: Someone finally speaks up to halt a torrent of talk.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'say when', the host's invitation to tell them when to stop pouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Said while a drink is poured, it marks the moment to stop.

clue.text: Laugh, almost catching end of joke

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word joke

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gets the punchline and laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laugh' is a horse's laugh: the sound a horse makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's whinny is its version of a laugh.

clue.text: Get me to look at play, a crude spectacle

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and watch a vulgar show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational, overacted entertainment with crude emotional appeal.

clue.text: Attempted coup in tea-growing area

parts.note: gunpowder is a Chinese green tea rolled into pellets
a plot is a patch of land for growing things

explanation.surface: A rebellion breaks out in a tea plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1605 Gunpowder Plot was Guy Fawkes's attempt to blow up Parliament, remembered on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 scheme to blow up the English Parliament and king was a failed seizure of power.
